parameters.query: SELECT id, name, ics_url FROM sources WHERE ics_url IS NOT NULL

nodes.name: Fetch ICS
nodes.notes: A dead or slow feed must not stall the other two sources' sync — continueRegularOutput sends an item with no usable body into Parse ICS events, which the parser below treats as zero events rather than throwing.

parameters.query:
INSERT INTO tasks (source_id, external_uid, task_text, type, due_at, starts_at, duration_minutes, origin)
SELECT $1::uuid, e->>'uid', e->>'summary', e->>'type', (e->>'due_at')::timestamptz, (e->>'starts_at')::timestamptz, (e->>'duration_minutes')::int, 'extracted'
FROM jsonb_array_elements($2::jsonb) AS e
ON CONFLICT (source_id, external_uid) WHERE external_uid IS NOT NULL DO UPDATE SET
  task_text = EXCLUDED.task_text,
  type = EXCLUDED.type,
  due_at = EXCLUDED.due_at,
  starts_at = EXCLUDED.starts_at,
  duration_minutes = EXCLUDED.duration_minutes;

nodes.name: Upsert tasks
nodes.notes: jsonb_array_elements('[]') yields zero rows, so an empty events array (dead feed, or Fetch ICS failed) is a harmless no-op rather than an error — this is what keeps the loop advancing even on a bad source.

parameters.query: UPDATE sources SET last_synced_at = now() WHERE id = $1::uuid

UPDATE tasks t SET course_id = c.id
FROM courses c
WHERE t.course_id IS NULL AND t.source_id = c.source_id AND c.is_active
  AND t.task_text ILIKE '%' || c.code || '%';

nodes.name: Link courses
nodes.notes: Naive substring match (ponytail: exact ILIKE, no fuzzy matching or normalisation) — a course code that never appears verbatim in the feed's SUMMARY is left course_id-null rather than guessed at. Upgrade path: normalise whitespace/case once a real feed shows this missing real matches.
